**Refined prompt:** Design (not implement) adding an `author` to comments in this NestJS/TypeORM RealWorld API — entity + relation, how it gets loaded, how it reaches the RO envelope as a spec-shaped profile, and the write path that sets it — answering as someone bound by this repo's conventions (envelope, nesting, layer order, mirror the sibling) and by LESSONS.md, with every claim about existing code cited to file:line, delivered as a design with decisions and consequences called out.

This is the blocked prerequisite in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` ("the comment case needs a `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet"), so I'm designing it as the unblock for the `DELETE .../comments/:id` ownership check as well as for spec conformance.

---

## 1. What exists today

| Thing | State | Cite |
|---|---|---|
| `Comment` entity | `id`, `body`, `@ManyToOne article` — **no author, no timestamps** | `src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` |
| `addComment` | sets `comment.body` only; never sees the caller | `src/article/article.service.ts:101-112` |
| `createComment` handler | no `@User('id')` param | `src/article/article.controller.ts:76-79` |
| `findComments` | loads whole article, returns `article.comments` raw | `src/article/article.service.ts:165-168` |
| `CommentsRO` | `comments: Comment[]` where the local `interface Comment` declares **only `body`** | `src/article/article.interface.ts:3-5, 20-22` |
| `deleteComment` | `commentRepository.findOne(id)` — no relations | `src/article/article.service.ts:114-129` |
| `ProfileData` (the shape `author` must be) | `{username, bio, image?, following?}` | `src/profile/profile.interface.ts:1-6` |
| `follows` lookup pattern to copy | `findProfile()` builds `ProfileData` by hand, sets `following` only `if (id)` | `src/profile/profile.service.ts:30-48` |

Useful: `ArticleModule` already registers `FollowsEntity` and `UserEntity` in `forFeature` (`src/article/article.module.ts:13`) and `ArticleService` already injects both repositories (`src/article/article.service.ts:20-23`). **No new module wiring is needed.**

---

## 2. The load strategy — the one decision that drives everything

**Recommendation: do NOT make `Comment.author` eager. Load it explicitly at the two sites that need it.**

The tempting option is `@ManyToOne(..., {eager: true})`, mirroring `ArticleEntity.comments` (`src/article/article.entity.ts:40`) — zero call-site changes. Reject it, because `ArticleEntity.comments` is eager, so every repository `findOne` path would then carry fully-hydrated `UserEntity` objects nested two deep — and `UserEntity` has a `password` column (`src/user/user.entity.ts:25-26`). These six methods all return `{article}` **unmapped, straight from the repository**:

`findOne` (`:96-99`), `addComment` (`:101-112`), `deleteComment` (`:114-129`), `favorite` (`:131-145`), `unFavorite` (`:147-163`), `update` (`:190-195`)

So eager-loading would put argon2 hashes into six existing responses in one line of entity change. `ProfileService` guards this by hand with `delete user.password` (`src/profile/profile.service.ts:26`) — there is no interceptor or `@Exclude()` anywhere in this repo to catch it, and introducing one would be inventing a pattern.

Not-eager confines the new data to exactly the paths that map it. The cost is the LESSONS rule *"a relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`"* — so the design must name every site that touches `comment.author` and give each one an explicit loader. That list is short and closed (§4).

*(Note for whoever implements: `findAll`/`findFeed` use `createQueryBuilder` (`:28-30`, `:75-77`), and TypeORM 0.2 does not apply eager relations to QueryBuilder results at all — which is why list responses have no comments today. So the eager-vs-not choice only ever affected the `findOne` paths above.)*

---

## 3. Entity change

```ts
// src/article/comment.entity.ts
@ManyToOne(type => UserEntity)
author: UserEntity;
```

- **Unidirectional** — no inverse `@OneToMany` on `UserEntity`. Both patterns exist in-repo (`ArticleEntity.author` has an inverse at `:37`, `UserEntity.favorites` has none at `:33-35`); nothing needs to navigate user → comments, so the inverse is dead weight.
- **Nullable, unavoidably.** `synchronize: true` and no migration files (`workspace.md:22`) means this column appears at boot; existing comment rows get `authorId = NULL`. There is no backfill mechanism in this repo short of hand SQL. So `author` may be null at the response boundary and the mapper must handle it — see §5.
- **New FK consequence:** `userRepository.delete({email})` (`src/user/user.service.ts:83-85`) is a raw DELETE, and `DELETE /users/:slug` is public and unguarded (`auth.md:47-49`). With an FK on `comment.authorId` it will now fail with a constraint error for any user who authored a comment. This is the *same* failure that already exists via `article.authorId` (`src/article/article.entity.ts:37`) — not a new class of bug, but a wider one.

---

## 4. Every site that touches `comment.author` (the closed list)

**a. Write — `addComment`** (`src/article/article.service.ts:101-112`)

Signature becomes `addComment(userId: number, slug: string, commentData: CreateCommentDto)`. Set `comment.author = await this.userRepository.findOne(userId)`.

Keep the field-by-field copy at `:105`. Do **not** `Object.assign(comment, commentData)` — `CreateCommentDto` carries no validators and there is no global pipe (`workspace.md:80-84`), so copying `body` by name is the only thing stopping a client from sending `{"comment": {"body": "x", "author": 7}}` and forging authorship (LESSONS #112).

**b. Controller — `createComment`** (`src/article/article.controller.ts:76-79`)

Add `@User('id') userId: number`. This route **is** in the middleware list (`src/article/article.module.ts:28`), so `userId` is always present — no optional-identity subtlety here.

**c. Read — `findComments`** (`src/article/article.service.ts:165-168`)

Replace the load-article-and-read-eager-comments approach with a direct query, mirroring the query-builder style already used at `:28-30`:

```ts
const comments = await this.commentRepository
  .createQueryBuilder('comment')
  .leftJoinAndSelect('comment.author', 'author')
  .where('comment.articleId = :id', { id: article.id })
  .getMany();
```

**d. Ownership read — `deleteComment`** (`src/article/article.service.ts:117`)

`this.commentRepository.findOne(id, { relations: ['author'] })`. Without this, `comment.author` is `undefined` and the ownership check silently compares against nothing — exactly LESSONS #6/#44.

Nothing else reads `comment.author`. Anyone adding a fifth site must add its own loader.

---

## 5. Response shape

`CommentsRO` currently declares `comments: Comment[]` against a local interface that has only `body` (`src/article/article.interface.ts:3-5`). That interface doesn't *filter* anything — the entity is what actually gets serialized, so responses today contain `id` and `body` despite the type. Replace it:

```ts
// src/article/article.interface.ts
import { ProfileData } from '../profile/profile.interface';

export interface CommentData {
  id: number;
  body: string;
  createdAt?: Date;
  updatedAt?: Date;
  author: ProfileData;
}
export interface CommentsRO { comments: CommentData[]; }
export interface CommentRO  { comment: CommentData; }   // spec shape for POST
```

Cross-module import is consistent with `article.service.ts:7` importing `FollowsEntity` from `../profile/`. Removing the local `Comment` interface also removes its name collision with the entity.

**Mapper lives in the service**, not the controller (layer order, `workspace.md:55-59`), mirroring how `ProfileService` hand-builds `ProfileData` (`src/profile/profile.service.ts:35-39`):

```ts
private toCommentData(comment: Comment, followingIds: Set<number> | null): CommentData {
  const a = comment.author;
  return {
    id: comment.id,
    body: comment.body,
    author: a && {
      username: a.username,
      bio: a.bio,
      image: a.image,
      ...(followingIds ? { following: followingIds.has(a.id) } : {}),
    },
  };
}
```

Two deliberate choices here:
- **`password` never enters `CommentData`** — this mapper is the only thing between `UserEntity` and the wire, which is why §2's not-eager decision matters.
- **`following` is omitted for anonymous callers**, matching `if (id) profile.following = ...` at `src/profile/profile.service.ts:43-45`. This diverges from the strict spec (which always has the boolean) but stays consistent with the sibling endpoint; if you'd rather be spec-exact, emit `following: false` and fix `findProfile` in the same pass rather than splitting the behaviour.

---

## 6. `following` on comment authors — two traps

**N+1 queries.** A per-comment `followsRepository.findOne` is N queries against a table with no FKs and no index on `(followerId, followingId)` (`schema.md:63-70`). Batch it once per request:

```ts
const ids = [...new Set(comments.map(c => c.author?.id).filter(Boolean))];
const follows = ids.length
  ? await this.followsRepository.find({ followerId: userId, followingId: In(ids) })
  : [];
const followingIds = new Set(follows.map(f => f.followingId));
```
(`In` from `typeorm`, already the import source at `article.service.ts:3`. Optional chaining is fine on TypeScript ^3.8.3, `package.json:47`.)

**`GET /articles/:slug/comments` is public** — it is not in the middleware list (`src/article/article.module.ts:23-31`, confirmed `auth.md:45-47`). Getting the caller's id therefore means `@User('id')`, which on an unguarded route calls `jwt.verify` itself (`src/user/user.decorator.ts:13-17`). That call is **not wrapped in try/catch**, so a stale or malformed token becomes a 500 instead of a 401 — LESSONS #79. Today this route never touches JWT at all, so adding `@User('id')` newly exposes it to that bug. Either fix the decorator's error translation as part of this change, or accept a known regression surface and note it. I'd fold the try/catch in; it's three lines and it's already an acknowledged defect.

---

## 7. What this unblocks (`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`)

With §4d in place, the ownership check has a line to point at — which is the whole test LESSONS #6 sets:

```ts
if (!comment.author || comment.author.id !== userId) {
  throw new HttpException('You are not the author of this comment.', HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN);
}
```

Requires `@User('id')` on `deleteComment` (`src/article/article.controller.ts:84-88`); that route is guarded (`src/article/article.module.ts:29`) so the id is present. Legacy `author === null` rows fail the check — deliberate: nobody can prove ownership of an orphaned comment.

Separately worth fixing in the same pass: `deleteComment` never verifies the comment belongs to `:slug`, and returns `{article}` with no error when the id isn't found (`src/article/article.service.ts:118-127`). Once it can 403, it should also 404.

---

## 8. Decisions I'd want your call on

1. **`POST /articles/:slug/comments` return shape.** It returns `{article}` today (`article.service.ts:111`); the spec says `{comment}`. Adding an author makes this the natural moment to switch to `CommentRO` — but it's a breaking change for anything reading `response.article`. Bundle it, or leave for the spec-conformance item?
2. **Bundle `createdAt`/`updatedAt` on `Comment`?** The spec's comment object has both and this entity has neither. Since `synchronize: true` means the entity change *is* the schema change, adding them in the same boot is nearly free — and doing it later is a second nullable-column-on-existing-rows episode. I'd bundle.
3. **`following` omitted vs always-false** for anonymous callers (§5).

## 9. Verification

Only `src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts` exists (`workspace.md:28`), so this is manual: register two users → A posts an article → B comments → `GET /articles/:slug/comments` **with no token** (expect `author` populated, no `following`, **no `password` anywhere**) → same with B's token (`following: false`) → with a token after B follows A → A attempts `DELETE` of B's comment (expect 403) → B deletes own (expect success) → `GET /articles/:slug` and confirm its `{article}` payload still contains no user objects.

**Not read:** `src/user/user.service.ts` beyond the `delete` method, `src/user/auth.middleware.ts`, `src/shared/pipes/validation.pipe.ts`, and the `prisma/` folder (explicitly out of scope per `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24`). One thing worth confirming empirically rather than trusting me on: I claim TypeORM 0.2.24 does not apply eager relations to `createQueryBuilder` results (§2) — if that's wrong, `findAll`'s articles already carry comments and the eager-author blast radius is wider than described, which only strengthens the not-eager recommendation.
